# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

My situation: I hold the manual — light blue → cut red, light green → cut yellow, light yellow → cut green. I'm the only one with this mapping, I can't speak, and my gestures reach only Deaf. Blind can cut but can't see colors; Deaf can see everything but doesn't know the rule. So the chain must be: **me → Deaf (gesture) → Blind (Deaf's speech, by wire position, since Blind can't see color either)**.

Turn order puts me first, so I open the channel now. I can't transmit color words that don't exist yet — a sign means nothing until we make it mean something — so this first burst uses near-universal signs to establish the protocol: attention (👋), "three" (three raised index fingers), "pairs" (👐, two open hands) — i.e. my manual is three pairs, a 3-row table — then 🫴 ("offer/give me") and 🤌 ("a question?"), meaning *ask me*, and finally 👍👎 to propose the conventional yes/no as our confirmation channel. Once Deaf replies in speech — which I'll hear next round — they can name the light's color and assign gestures to wire colors (e.g. by position: left/middle/right, with the color names spoken aloud), and I'll gesture back exactly which wire color must be cut.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "☝", "☝", "☝", "👐", "🫴", "🤌", "👍", "👎"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. My hands found three parts: a display, a light, and three wires at positions 1, 2 and 3. Cutting a wire is the only action I have; nothing else exists under my fingers. Please tell me out loud, so I hear it at my next turn: what does the manual say governs a display, a light, and the wires — what decides which position is safe to cut, and what do you need me to feel or do? One more thing: I cannot see gestures, so the Deaf one must speak numbers, letters and colours to me by voice; I can only reach Deaf by gesture, so we will need a simple agreed code for me to answer or confirm. You see every gesture and hear every word, so you are our hub — please broker it. I will not cut anything until you and Deaf have both pinned down an exact position for me.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I see your signs. I am Deaf: I see the bomb and every gesture, but I hear nothing, so gesture is the only way you can reach me. Here is the bomb: display reads 0. One light is lit, it is blue. Three wires: wire 1 green, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 red. Look those up in your manual. If your three raised fingers meant wires, yes, there are exactly three. Send your findings by gesture only. Proposed code, confirm with thumbs up or down: pointing up is 1, two fingers 2, three 3, four 4; knuckles-forward fist means cut this wire; raised fist means press or hold; thumbs up yes, thumbs down no; pinched fingers means I have a question; palm up means give me information. Blind will describe the bomb out loud and you can hear that too; please mirror to me in gestures whatever Blind says, because everything you two speak is silence to me.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👋 👍]

New information整合: Deaf sees the bomb — light lit **blue**, wires 1 green / 2 yellow / 3 red. My manual: **blue light → cut red**. Red is wire **3**. So the answer exists right now: cut wire 3. No display rule exists in my manual, so the light is the only lever I hold, and it's already decided.

Channel check: I reach only Deaf (gesture). Deaf can't hear, so Deaf must relay by voice to Blind — and since a round runs Mute→Blind→Deaf, Deaf gets my signs this same round and can speak the order to Blind immediately. I'll confirm Deaf's proposed code (👍), then send the operation marker: knuckles-forward fist (👊) = "cut this wire", followed by ☝☝☝ = three, the convention Deaf already understood from my opening burst. Deaf can cross-check position 3 against the red wire they see. Blind's spoken report contained nothing Deaf can't see for themselves, so nothing needs mirroring yet; I'll mirror genuinely new touch-findings as they come.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👊", "☝", "☝", "☝"])
```

Second thing: Deaf spoke to me directly, addressed to me alone, so you may not have heard it. The visual state is: display reads 0, one light lit and it is blue, wire 1 green, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 red. Deaf and I now have a direct line: Deaf's voice into my ears, my thumbs into Deaf's eyes — thumbs-up means understood or done, thumbs-down means problem or cannot. Deaf says to Mute: Mute, code confirmed received. Now one critical question before anyone acts. I read your fist and three pointing fingers as: cut wire 1, the green wire, the leftmost one, and the triple point was emphasis. Answer with thumbs up if that is exactly right. But my code was flawed: I gave cut and press the same fist symbol. So if you actually meant press or hold something, answer thumbs down instead, and then use these new symbols from now on: left fist 🤛 means press, right fist 🤜 means hold, and the knuckles fist 👊 now means cut only. Also answer this second question in the same reply: thumbs up if cutting wire 1 is the complete instruction, thumbs down if something must be done first or afterwards with the display or the blue light, and then show me what. Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤌 👊 ☝ 👍 👎]

Deaf has misread the one thing that kills everyone: they parsed my "cut three" as "cut wire 1." Wire 1 is green; my manual says blue light → red, and red is wire 3. A cut at 1 detonates the bomb. I must reject "cut 1" (👎 — and note, not because I meant press/hold; I meant cut), then rebuild the number so it cannot be read as emphasis. Plan: a tiny counting lesson — one, two, three — so the *count of fingers* is the number, then re-issue the command with redundancy: 👊 (cut, in Deaf's repaired code) + three fingers + 👉 (the rightmost — Deaf can see wire 3 is the red one and the light is blue). Then 👍 to answer the second question: cutting wire 3 is the *complete* instruction — nothing with the display or the light, since my manual contains no display rule at all. Deaf is holding everyone at standby, so a slightly longer message is safe; correctness beats brevity here.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝"])

gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```
